classification.difficultyReason: The hardest part requires recognising a perimeter formed by a major arc and its chord, deriving the three-quarter circumference, and combining it with a Pythagorean chord length. Other parts require symmetry or base differences before assembling perimeters.

content.prompt: Find the missing sides, then find the perimeter. Round your answer to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Isosceles trapezium with dashed perpendicular heights, matched sloping sides, and unknown right offset x and sloping side y.
spec.mathematics: Parallel bases 7.2 m and 12.8 m; height 4.5 m; equal legs imply each horizontal offset is half the base difference. No right-angle markers are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible; no calculated lengths or perimeter.

answer.worked:
The equal sloping sides give equal horizontal offsets.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{12.8-7.2}{2}\\x&=2.8\,\mathrm{m}\\y&=\sqrt{4.5^2+2.8^2}\\y&=\sqrt{28.09}\\y&=5.3\,\mathrm{m}\\P&=7.2+12.8+2(5.3)\\P&=30.6\,\mathrm{m}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right trapezium with two left right-angle markers and an unlabelled sloping right side.
spec.mathematics: Height 21 cm; parallel bases 20 cm and 32 cm. The missing leg has horizontal displacement 12 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Given lengths only; no added construction line, unknown label or calculated answer.

answer.worked:
The horizontal difference between the bases is $32-20=12\,\mathrm{cm}$. Let $s$ be the sloping side.
$$\begin{align*}s&=\sqrt{21^2+12^2}\\s&=\sqrt{585}\,\mathrm{cm}\\s&\approx24.2\,\mathrm{cm}\\P&=21+20+32+\sqrt{585}\\P&\approx97.2\,\mathrm{cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontal kite with dashed perpendicular diagonals, single ticks on the two left sides and double ticks on the two right sides.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal half-diagonal lengths 40 cm and 12 cm; upper vertical half 9 cm. Equal side pairs imply the lower vertical half also measures 9 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens, constructions and equality marks only; no calculated side lengths.

answer.short: Left sides: $41.0\,\mathrm{cm}$ each; right sides: $15.0\,\mathrm{cm}$ each; $P=112.0\,\mathrm{cm}$.
answer.worked:
The equal side pairs give equal upper and lower vertical half-diagonals. Let $l$ and $r$ be a left and right side.
$$\begin{align*}l&=\sqrt{40^2+9^2}\\l&=41\,\mathrm{cm}\\r&=\sqrt{12^2+9^2}\\r&=15\,\mathrm{cm}\\P&=2(41)+2(15)\\P&=112.0\,\mathrm{cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A three-quarter-circle major arc closed by a chord; dashed equal radii meet at a marked right angle.
spec.mathematics: Radius 13 mm; minor central angle 90 degrees; boundary contains a 270-degree arc and the chord of the right triangle formed by the radii.
spec.answerVisibility: The radius, equal-radius ticks and central right angle are permanent givens; chord length and perimeter are withheld.

answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the straight side and $L$ the major arc length. The arc is three quarters of the circumference.
$$\begin{align*}s&=\sqrt{13^2+13^2}\\s&=13\sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{mm}\\s&\approx18.4\,\mathrm{mm}\\L&=\frac34\times2\pi\times13\\L&=19.5\pi\,\mathrm{mm}\\P&=13\sqrt{2}+19.5\pi\\P&\approx79.6\,\mathrm{mm}\end{align*}$$
